:::{#rem-logarithm-formula}
#### The logarithm to base $b$ through the natural logarithm

For each $x > 0$, exactly one $y$ satisfies @def-logarithm,
and
$$\log_b x = \frac{\logf{x}}{\logf{b}}.$$

To see why,
note that by @def-real-power, $b^y = \expf{y \cd \logf{b}}$,
so we need $\expf{y \cd \logf{b}} = x$.
If $y \cd \logf{b} = \logf{x}$,
then $\expf{y \cd \logf{b}} = \expf{\logf{x}} = x$,
by part 1 of @thm-exp-log-inverse.
Conversely, if $\expf{y \cd \logf{b}} = x$,
then applying $\logt$ to both sides gives
$y \cd \logf{b} = \logf{x}$,
by part 2 of @thm-exp-log-inverse.
Since $b \ne 1$,
$\logf{b} \ne 0$,
so we can divide by it,
and $y = \frac{\logf{x}}{\logf{b}}$ is the only solution.

:::
